variants.title: Faraday: a 100-turn coil and a steel bar magnet
variants.sample: Coil of 100 turns, radius 2 cm; steel bar magnet
variants.unknown: k = peak emf / speed for the 100-turn coil
variants.note: Half the turns of the standard coil: every turn adds the same emf, so k should be half as large.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XII, Ch 6 Electromagnetic Induction (emf = −N dΦ/dt)
source.note: Generic school coil; the turns are printed on its base.

variants.title: Faraday: a 500-turn coil and a steel bar magnet
variants.sample: Coil of 500 turns, radius 2 cm; steel bar magnet
variants.unknown: k = peak emf / speed for the 500-turn coil
variants.note: Two and a half times the turns of the standard coil, so two and a half times the emf at every speed.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XII, Ch 6 Electromagnetic Induction (emf = −N dΦ/dt)
source.note: Generic school coil; the turns are printed on its base.

variants.title: Faraday: a wider coil (radius 3 cm)
variants.sample: Coil of 200 turns, radius 3 cm; steel bar magnet
variants.unknown: k = peak emf / speed for the 3 cm coil
variants.note: For a small magnet on the axis the peak emf falls as 1 / a²: the wider coil gives less than half the emf of the 2 cm coil.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XII, Ch 6 Electromagnetic Induction
source.note: Axial field of a dipole B = μ0 m / (2π z³) far away; the kernel uses the exact on-axis flux μ0 m a² / 2(a² + z²)^1.5 per turn.

variants.title: Faraday: a narrower coil (radius 1.5 cm)
variants.sample: Coil of 200 turns, radius 1.5 cm; steel bar magnet
variants.unknown: k = peak emf / speed for the 1.5 cm coil
variants.note: A narrow coil sits closer to the magnet: the peak emf grows as 1 / a², about 1.8 times that of the 2 cm coil.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XII, Ch 6 Electromagnetic Induction
source.note: The magnet (12 mm square) still passes through the narrower former.

variants.title: Faraday: a ferrite (ceramic) bar magnet
variants.sample: Coil of 200 turns, radius 2 cm; ferrite (ceramic) bar magnet
variants.unknown: k = peak emf / speed with the ferrite magnet
variants.note: A hard ferrite has remanence Br of about 0.39 T, so a 50 × 12 × 12 mm bar has a moment m ≈ Br V / μ0 ≈ 2.2 A·m².

source.title: IEC 60404-8-1 magnetically hard materials: hard ferrite, Br about 0.38-0.40 T
source.note: m = Br V / μ0 with V = 7.2 cm³; a real bar works a little below Br.

variants.title: Faraday: a neodymium (NdFeB) bar magnet
variants.sample: Coil of 200 turns, radius 2 cm; neodymium (NdFeB) bar magnet
variants.unknown: k = peak emf / speed with the NdFeB magnet
variants.note: Grade N35 NdFeB has Br of about 1.17-1.22 T, so a 50 × 12 × 12 mm bar has m ≈ 6.8 A·m²: about seven times the steel magnet, and the galvanometer needs a coarser range.

source.title: IEC 60404-8-1 magnetically hard materials: NdFeB grade N35, Br about 1.17-1.22 T
source.note: m = Br V / μ0 with V = 7.2 cm³.
